A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMOD research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RMOD experiments on HH, UltraFeedback and ValuePrism, including reward comparisons, ablations, latency measurements and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional distillation, GPT-4o evaluation, KL-divergence and latency results.

M1.justification: The central maxmin decoding procedure remains, but v2 introduces DISTILL-RMOD, a policy trained by supervised fine-tuning on RMOD-generated responses. Appendix C.1 also changes UltraFeedback's value architecture from five separately trained models to one model with five outputs. These are substantive procedural and architectural changes.

E1.justification: The same three datasets remain. Within UltraFeedback, v2 replaces the conciseness objective with safety and adds a four-objective scenario excluding safety to examine positively correlated objectives. Coverage changes are confined to task variants within an existing dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds MAXMIN-GRPO, shown as the Maxmin GRPO bar, providing a robust fine-tuning comparator. UltraFeedback's CONCISENESS comparator is replaced by INSTRUCTION-FOLLOWING and SAFETY. Table 3 adds direct-reward best-of-K comparisons, including WORSTCASE selection. The CD- prefixes merely rename existing controlled-decoding baselines.

E3.justification: Reported UltraFeedback settings change from four to sixteen training responses per prompt and from 956 to 1000 test prompts; Figure 4 changes from worst-case win rate to reward improvement. v2 also introduces separate GPT-4o grading for helpfulness and harmlessness, KL estimation protocols, and length-normalized HH latency measurements on a 40GB A100. The original UltraFeedback latency protocol remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds the correlated-objective ablation, KL-divergence analysis, and direct-reward best-of-K sweeps examining reward overoptimization. It updates weight-trajectory examples and replaces the UltraFeedback conciseness case study with two HH cases. Existing block-size, lambda, ValuePrism reverse-order and UltraFeedback latency analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions display error bars without explaining their construction and retain the same unelaborated latency-significance statement. v2's additional error bars accompany revised or new results; it does not document new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 replaces UltraFeedback results under changed objectives and settings, so these do not establish a same-setting improvement over v1. It adds substantial results: Table 1 reports GPT-4o worst-case win rates of 59.1% for RMOD, 57.9% for DISTILL-RMOD and 57.6% for CD-UNIFORM. Tables 2-4 add latency, direct-reward best-of-K and KL results, alongside new ablation and qualitative findings.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix D's alternative Hedge-BR treatment is removed, including payoff definitions, update derivations, an O(1/sqrt(I)) approximate-equilibrium guarantee and comparisons with gradient descent. The central RMOD proofs and KKT analysis remain in Appendices A-B. v2 additionally formalizes the MAXMIN-GRPO objective and updates in Appendix C.1.

C1.justification: The principal claims about robust inference-time alignment, convex weight optimization, analytic best responses and efficient blockwise decoding remain. v2 adds an abstract-level effectiveness claim for the distilled policy and extends its headline empirical claims to LLM-as-Judge evaluation, without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 argues that RMOD also works with positively correlated objectives, attributes high-K deterioration of some best-of-K baselines to reward overoptimization, and interprets distillation performance alongside policy divergence. Its qualitative explanations shift from conciseness to helpfulness and safety. It also removes v1's explicit concluding limitation about reward bias and value-function accuracy.

D1.justification: v2 documents distillation using 16000 HH prompts and three training epochs, the MAXMIN-GRPO implementation, approximate training/evaluation times, and additional hardware settings. Appendix C.5 supplies complete separate GPT-4o judging prompts and evaluation instructions. These materially expand reproducibility information; the repository URL itself is unchanged.

R1.justification: The main positioning within robust multi-objective alignment remains. v2 adds discussion of Transfer Q-star, Chehade et al.'s constrained inference-time alignment and Yoon et al.'s robust best-of-K work, and distinguishes objective robustness from MAXMIN-RLHF's user-group robustness. References supporting the removed preference-history motivation and no-regret discussion are dropped.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around balancing critical objectives. Related Work becomes a separate section, the method exposition centers on one practical algorithm, blockwise decoding moves earlier, and the experimental appendix is extensively reorganized. Acknowledgement and reproducibility statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 changes document typography and page layout, condenses two algorithm displays into one, adds four tables, expands Figure 2 and redraws UltraFeedback plots with different axes and legends. v1's paired ValuePrism figure is split between the main text and appendix, and judging prompts and response examples receive boxed displays.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily assesses alignment using the reward models driving optimization. v2 substantially strengthens validation through separate GPT-4o judging, direct investigation of reward overoptimization and a robust fine-tuning comparator. Distillation, latency and KL analyses also make practical tradeoffs more assessable, with fuller implementation and judging details. These gains outweigh removal of the optional Hedge-BR discussion and explicit concluding caveat, while the central proofs remain. The added judge comparisons still lack uncertainty estimates, and revised UltraFeedback results cannot establish gains over v1 under identical conditions.
